extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy members, artists, music industry professionals, and the general public interested in GRAMMY rules
extracted.subtask_description: Official GRAMMY Awards rules and category-definition updates for the 63rd Annual GRAMMYs, describing renamed categories, category definitions, Best New Artist eligibility rules, nominations committee conflict rules, and the rule-change process. Intended to inform members, nominees, and the public about how entries and committee participation will be judged/managed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Progressive R&B Album (formerly Best Urban Contemporary Album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Urban Contemporary Album has been renamed Best Progressive R&B Album. This category is intended to highlight albums that include the more progressive elements of R&B and may include samples and elements of hip-hop, rap, dance, and electronic music. It may also incorporate production elements found in pop, euro-pop, country, rock, folk and alternative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change includes a more accurate definition to describe the merit or characteristics of music compositions or performances themselves within the genre of R&B; intended to better categorize and describe this subgenre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Melodic Rap Performance (formerly Best Rap/Sung Performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Best Rap/Sung Performance has been renamed Best Melodic Rap Performance. This category is intended to recognize solo and collaborative performances containing elements of rap and melody over modern production. This performance requires a strong and clear presence of melody combined with rap cadence, and is inclusive of dialects, lyrics or performance elements from non-rap genres including R&B, rock, country, electronic or more. The production may include traditional elements of rap or elements characteristic of the aforementioned non-rap genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renaming represents inclusivity of the growing hybrid performance trends within the rap genre; emphasizes both melodic presence and rap cadence as evaluative features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Latin Pop Or Urban Album (renamed from Latin Pop Album)
rubrics_metrics.description: Latin Pop Album has been renamed Best Latin Pop Or Urban Album. The category is intended to recognize excellence in Latin pop or urban music recordings that utilize a stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content, and/or musical presentation to create a sensibility that reflects the broad spectrum of Latin pop music style and culture. The category includes recordings from balladeers and commercial Latin music and is not limited to any one region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renaming/migration reflects prominence of Latin urban genres and broadens the category to encompass pop and urban stylistic approaches across regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Latin Rock Or Alternative Album (renamed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Latin Rock, Urban Or Alternative Album has been renamed Best Latin Rock Or Alternative Album. The category is intended to highlight Latin rock or alternative music recordings that utilize a stylistic intention, song structure, lyrical content and/or musical presentation to create a sensibility that reflects the broad spectrum of the Latin music style and culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refocuses category naming/definition to better represent Latin rock and alternative recordings and their stylistic/structural merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist — removal of a maximum releases cap and screening committee role
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no longer a specified maximum number of releases prohibiting artists from entering the Best New Artist category. Screening committees will be charged with determining whether the artist had attained a breakthrough or prominence prior to the eligibility year; such a determination would result in disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is now more qualitative/committee-driven regarding prior prominence rather than strictly numeric maximum releases; screening committees evaluate breakthrough/prominence and can disqualify accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist — minimum release requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum required is five singles or tracks or a complete album. (There is no maximum requirement.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric floor for eligibility; artists must have at least five singles/tracks or a full album to meet the baseline for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist — prior submission limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An artist cannot have submitted for Best New Artist more than three times previously, whether as a new artist or as a solo artist who emerged from a group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps the number of prior submissions (three) across solo/group histories to limit repeated attempts at Best New Artist consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist — prior nomination exclusion and two exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Artists cannot have been previously nominated as a performer — whether as a solo act or as part of a group. Exceptions: (1) If an artist was nominated as a featured artist before the artist had released at least five singles or an entire album, they are eligible. (2) New for the 2026 GRAMMYs: artists who were nominated in Album Of The Year but whose contributions fell below the current 20 percent playing time threshold are now eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how prior nominations affect eligibility and provides two concrete exceptions (featured-artist pre-eligibility and Album Of The Year contributions under the 20% playing-time threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Best New Artist — eligibility for new duos/groups and artists from other disciplines; explicit exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: New established duos/groups consisting of former solo artists or former group members — provided that none of the previous solo artists nor the duo/group had attained prominence — are eligible. New recording artists who previously achieved recognition in a different discipline, such as songwriters, politicians, actors, etc., are also eligible. Not eligible for Best New Artist are artists who have been credited only as featured artists and choirs, choruses and large band ensembles of 16 or more members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines pathways into eligibility (new formations, cross-discipline entrants) while listing categories explicitly excluded; screening for prior prominence applies to former members/acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominations Review Committees — conflict of interest disclosure and recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of invitation to participate on a Nominations Review Committee, a conflict of interest disclosure form will be provided. Each invitee must disclose whether, in connection with any recording that may be entered in the current year’s process, (a) the person would be in line to receive a GRAMMY nomination or win for any recordings being considered in a particular category, (b) the person would have any direct or indirect financial ties to the recordings or creators under consideration, (c) the person has immediate familial ties to any of the artists in the top voter selections, and/or (d) any other conflict of interest, actual or perceived. If a recording listed by the invitee presents a conflict of interest, the Academy will notify the committee member that they cannot participate that year. If a conflict is discovered during the committee meeting, that person will be notified and recused from the meeting. Failure to voluntarily disclose any conflict of interest will result in the person being barred from future Nominations Review Committee participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory disclosure at invitation; proactive barring if conflict exists; in-meeting discovery leads to immediate recusal; non-disclosure leads to future participation ban.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule change proposal and ratification process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy accepts proposals for rule changes from members of the music community throughout the year that are carefully reviewed and, if accepted, ultimately ratified at the annual Board meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural pathway for how rules are proposed and become effective: submission by members → review → Board ratification; changes announced may go into effect immediately for the specified GRAMMY Awards cycle.
